title: The Broken Seal
description: You are Officer Alex Morgan, Unit 12. A delivery van has struck a bollard on Harbor Road. Check your vehicle, take your field kit, and call dispatch. A routine response is only as good as the details you notice.

entities.label: Unit 12
entities.blocked: Inspect the vehicle, collect your field kit, and acknowledge dispatch first.

message: Tires, lights, brakes. Unit 12 is serviceable.
Camera, evidence bags, gloves and first-aid supplies.

dispatch.blocked: Inspect Unit 12 and collect the field kit from its trunk first.
message: Unit 12, delivery van into a bollard outside the Lantern Diner. Check for injuries. Harbor Road, eastbound.

arrive.blocked: Acknowledge the assignment on the radio first.
message: A broken seal, a shaken driver. Start by making the scene safe.
Warning lamps on. Cones protect the loading apron.

aid.blocked: Secure the scene with warning lights and cones first.
message: Nora is shaken but alert. No immediate injury. Medical assistance has been requested.

driver.blocked: Check Nora for injuries before asking about the collision.
message: “A man pulled a crate from the van. I tried to follow him in the mirror and clipped the bollard. He went toward Pier 04.”
“Orange work jacket. Handcart. I saw him break the seal before the van moved. Didn’t see his face.”

records.blocked: Record both statements and recover the seal and manifest before asking dispatch to corroborate the case.
message: Dispatch is comparing the recovered cargo documentation and independent accounts.

backup.blocked: Corroborate the cargo evidence with dispatch first.
message: Unit 8 is approaching the pier. Hold your position; give the contractor space.

backupArrive.blocked: No support unit has been requested.
message: Officer Chen is holding the exit. You have time to talk.

introduce.blocked: Establish the evidence behind this contact first.
message: Ellis says he was returning damaged equipment. Listen, then compare his account to the evidence.

present.blocked: Introduce yourself and ask for Ellis’s account first.
message: The matching seal and signed manifest contradict the return story. Ellis admits taking the crate.

calm.blocked: Hear his account and explain the matching seal and manifest first.
message: Ellis has put his hands up. Move close and apply restraints.

pressure.blocked: Establish the evidence first. Once Ellis cooperates or stops running, give him a way to cooperate.

effects.reason: Premature pressure led to a pursuit.

message: Ellis bolts toward the closed freight gate. Follow at a safe distance and speak to him when he stops.

cuff.blocked: Get Ellis to cooperate before applying restraints.
message: Restraints secured and checked. Complete the custody check before transport.
No weapon found. Personal items recorded for safekeeping.
You explain the reason for arrest and the right to remain silent and obtain counsel.

escort.blocked: Complete the custody check, explain the caution, and recover the radio crate before transport.
message: Ellis is secured in the rear seat. Return to the harbor duty office.

return.blocked: Secure Ellis in the rear seat first.
message: Park, step out, and submit the custody and evidence record.

book.blocked: Bring the suspect and all three exhibits back to the duty office.
message: Custody accepted. Three exhibits logged. The missing emergency equipment is recovered.
Fresh handcart tracks turn off the road toward Pier 04.
The van belongs to the authorized delivery company. Nora’s account is consistent with the vehicle record.
Check your surroundings. Reverse away, or recover the vehicle through the field tools.
Ellis will follow you. Recover the crate and lead him to Unit 12.
Dispatch has your assignment. Bring the completed case and all exhibits here at the end of your shift.

seal.title: Broken cargo seal
seal.detail: A numbered blue security seal. Cut cleanly, before the collision. Serial HN–407 matches a crate of harbor emergency radios.

manifest.title: Delivery manifest
manifest.detail: Four emergency-radio kits for the harbor office. All four left the depot sealed. Delivery signed by contractor Ellis Vale; one crate is missing.

cargo.title: Missing radio crate
cargo.detail: An open crate holding the missing emergency-radio kit. The remaining half of seal HN–407 fits the piece recovered at the van.

cargo-record.text: HN–407 is assigned to four emergency-radio kits. One is unaccounted for. Ellis Vale signed the delivery. Harbor security has opened the Pier 04 gate.

params.startText: Ellis bolts toward the closed freight gate. Keep him in sight.
params.corneredText: Ellis has reached the closed freight gate. Approach and return to a calm conversation.

text.text: “He cut the seal and wheeled a crate away. Orange jacket, heading for Pier 04. I looked back and hit the bollard.”
“I’m okay. More embarrassed than anything. But something’s missing from the van.”
“My hands are still shaking. Is everyone okay?” Start with her wellbeing. Questions can wait until the scene is safe.

choices.label: Check for injuries and request medical help
Ask what happened before the collision

text.text: “He broke that blue seal before the van moved. Orange work jacket. Went through the freight yard. But I can’t identify his face.” His account corroborates the direction of travel. Clothing alone is not identification.
“Been waiting for my coffee. Saw something odd at the back of that van.” Give him room to describe what he actually saw.

choices.label: Ask him to describe what he saw

text.text: “I took one crate. I was going to sell it. It was a stupid decision. Please… don’t make this worse.”
“Just returning damaged equipment. Nothing to do with that van. I was leaving, actually.”
“There’s nowhere else to go, is there?”
